LOCATION: stacks where the call number points at a gap and the book is on the cart one aisle over
returns cart parked spine-in against the wall, its far side never seen
circulation desk with a rubber stamp that says MISSING and a drawer of slips no one filled in yet
branch library open one summer with one keeper, every shelf walked twice
lost-and-found bin that holds everything except what was asked for, until you turn it over
reading room where a stranger who has never touched paper reviews every page
ANTAGONIST: the label written before the search
the confident word from someone who has never held the thing
the gap that looks like an absence
the send button that sits closer than the shelf
MACGUFFIN: the book on the shelf below
the transit slip filled in by a student's hand
the receipt that says where it was read
THREAT: a MISSING tag read by the next patron before anyone checks
being corrected after the send instead of before it
trusting an outside reader because it is outside, not because it has seen
the search that would have taken one minute, skipped
CHARACTER: the specialist who checks above, below, the carts, and then walks around them
the student helper who stops at the gap and learns to keep looking
the stranger with no eyes who answers anyway
the patron who has been waiting for this one book all week
